summary: 60-foot steel tower on Quartz Peak in Kootenai National Forest, Lincoln County, Montana; cabin burned 1954, tower abandoned after the late 1960s, now reached by a 5-mile trail.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower, built in 1935 after a cabin was begun in 1934; the cabin burned in 1954

staffing.status: in use until the late 1960s; no staffing details in the sources read

visit.trail_note: The road to the summit is gone; a July 2026 trip report describes a 5-mile foot trail with about 800 feet of climbing

events.note: Cabin begun on the summit; the first structure
The cabin burned down; the tower was not destroyed
Tower in use until the late 1960s, abandoned since. Sources say only 'late 1960s', so 1968 is an approximate year
Registered January 9, 2021 as US 1509, MT 87; nominated by Kyle Stetler

corrections.why: The NHLR description and the 2026 trip report both say the cabin burned in 1954, while the tower stayed in use until the late 1960s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 6,251 ft (1,905 m) and firelookout.com gives 6,255 ft. The record's 1,905.3 m matches NHLR; the gap is about 4 feet and was not resolved further.

sources.title: Libby to Canada - Land of the Lookouts | MTBDR #8

notes_for_editor: Standing status rests on the FFLA Montana list and NHLR's description; the only account of the site today is one July 2026 trip report, which does not say whether the tower was climbed or what condition it is in. No source states public access or rental, so access is left out of facts. The late-1960s dates are approximate ('late 1960s' only); 1968 is an approximate year. The corrections entry covers the record's bare '1954 burned'. No photo URL was found; firelookout.com credits a photo to Gary Weber, but the page text gives no image link.
